articles.body: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 more years in prison on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers, a court summary said. Wong, 30, pleaded guilty in September to seeking foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China under Beijing’s national security law, having spent nearly six years imprisoned.

"This is a once-in-a-generation event." But electoral breadth presents a governing dilemma. articles.body: Following a resounding Midterm election defeat, Is MAGA Losing Its Grip on the Republican Party? Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Bryan Lanza, Republican strategist and Partner in Mercury's Washington DC office. "The big thing about MAGA was confrontation, in your face," explained Lanza. But following a veritable blue wave, he believes the electorate has delivered a warning: "We need to move beyond that." While Donald Trump has acknowledged the Democratic victory, at times combative, at times conciliatory, Lanza argues that the president must begin his final two years in office reversing damaging tariffs, addressing widespread dissatisfaction with immigration enforcement and navigating a highly unpopular Iran war.

articles.body: Does an electoral repudiation of Donald Trump also mark the beginning of MAGA’s decline? Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Ian Reifowitz, SUNY Distinguished Professor of Historical Studies at Empire State University, who describes the Republican defeat as “an absolute and complete repudiation” of the president. He connects voters’ economic frustrations with resentment over presidential enrichment, while questioning whether ideological differences between progressive and moderate Democrats proved decisive. Looking towards 2028, Reifowitz identifies a central Republican dilemma: “If JD Vance is the nominee, he can’t run against Donald Trump”, yet Trump himself may refuse to relinquish control of the party.
articles.headline: 'Is Republican Party able to pivot away from MAGA movement, or will it sputter forward leaderless?'

articles.body: AUSTIN — Texas. Florida. Pennsylvania. Colorado. Arizona. Nevada. California. The historic landslide of Latino voters toward Democrats hit battleground after battleground Tuesday, crumbling the coalition that helped carry President Donald Trump to victory just one cycle ago. “This is an earthquake,” Democratic Latino operative Sergio Gonzalez told POLITICO on the sidelines of Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa’s victory party in Austin. “Latinos were angry. They were angry this election.” While the entire country shifted toward Democrats, nowhere shifted as dramatically as predominantly Latino areas. Across the nation Latino voters of all backgrounds — Mexican Americans and Central Americans in the Southwest, heartland and on the West Coast, Puerto Ricans and Dominicans in Pennsylvania, Venezuelans, Puerto Ricans and Cubans in Florida — unhappy with the economy and furious over Trump’s immigration enforcement fled the party in droves. In a single cycle, Democrats appeared to reset Republicans’ gradual decade-long gains with Latino voters. Latino voters who “broke for President Trump in historical numbers [in 2024] … had to make a hard change because their paycheck wasn't moving fast and far enough for them,” said Trump’s former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer in an interview Tuesday night. “And Republicans ran out of runway on that.” The epicenter of the earthquake was Texas, where a turnout surge — especially among younger first-time Latino voters — helped Democrats sweep Texas’ statewide offices — the first time since 1994 they’ve won any at all. Republicans won only one of the five House seats they had gerrymandered. “What we're seeing today is a political realignment,” said Democratic Rep. Henry Cuellar, who romped to a 30-point victory Tuesday night in a newly redrawn district Trump carried by double digits two years ago. “Republicans were renting the Hispanic vote — yet governed like they owned it,” said Giancarlo Sopo, the GOP strategist behind Trump’s viral 2020 Spanish-language campaign jingle . But Democrats have been here before. Then President Barack Obama and his Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton posted similarly strong numbers with Latinos, before Trump’s blue-collar populism helped break through for the GOP. Some Democrats warn that their party should not misread this week’s results to assume that Latinos are once again loyal Democratic voters. “Tonight ought to scare the hell out of both political parties,” said Javier Palomarez, president and CEO of the U.S. Hispanic Business Council, on Tuesday. “Americans are running out of patience, and the politicians who keep mistaking their votes for unconditional loyalty are going to find themselves unemployed." Latinos’ swing right two years ago had been fueled by frustration over inflation combined with some voters’ dissatisfaction with the Biden administration’s border policy. A cycle earlier, in 2020, Trump made significant inroads in Florida and Texas as well. But growing economic woes under Trump, combined with his hardline interior immigration enforcement, swung those communities hard this time around. “In the Hispanic community, the hyper-aggressive ICE raids, I think, will go down as one of the darkest blemishes in modern history,” Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez, who cruised to reelection Tuesday in a seat Trump had won by 10 points, told POLITICO Tuesday night. “The American people are struggling right now, and and and they delivered a very heavy punishment at the ballot box today.” Heavily Latino counties swung more toward Democrats than any other type of place, according to preliminary returns. A handful of counties in Texas that are more than 90 percent Latino swung more than 25 points toward Democrats from 2024, the results show. Latino-majority Miami-Dade County in South Florida swung nearly 20 points.If current results hold, roughly half of the 10 Latino Republicans who served in the last Congress won’t be returning, while Democrats’ Latino caucus will grow significantly. “We put in the hard work. Talk to Latino voters early and often, and they're showing up,” Rep. Linda Sanchez (D-Calif.), who chairs the Congressional Hispanic Caucus’ BOLD PAC, told POLITICO. “They trust Democrats more on the economy now. They see us as real champions and fighters.” Trump won Starr County, Texas — part of Cuellar’s district — with 58 percent of the vote two years ago, the first time in more than a century that a Republican had won a presidential election there. On Tuesday, Democrat James Talarico won 77 percent there. That county, like many others in the Rio Grande Valley, had long favored Democrats but moved toward the GOP during the Trump era. That’s now all been erased, as Brownsville native Gina Hinojosa will become the first Hispanic governor of Texas since it became a U.S. state. “We've called the RGV a bellwether for so long,” Melissa Morales, the executive director of SOMOS PAC, told POLITICO. “But to actually get the first Latina governor of Texas from the RGV I think is a bellwether in its own of what the next generation of leadership looks like.” In California’s 22nd District, a Central Valley district which is roughly three-quarters Latino, progressive Democrat Randy Villegas was leading incumbent GOP Rep. David Valadao 66%-34% with roughly two-thirds of the vote in. A handful of rural majority-Latino counties in Kansas — Seward, Finney and Ford — that Trump had won by more than 30 points in 2024 were narrowly won by Democratic Senate candidate Adam Hamilton. The counties were among those shaken by ICE raids earlier in the fall. “Recent ICE activity in southwest Kansas turned around the electorate out here,” said Republican state Sen. Bill Clifford, who represents Finney County. The results are a vindication for Democrats who’ve been clamoring for more investment into Latino voters. “I think this would be a wake-up call to the Democratic Party in general that investing in Latino outreach, communication, and good candidates makes a big difference, especially in areas that you think were considered red back in the day,” Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) told POLITICO Tuesday night.
articles.headline: ‘This is an earthquake’: Latino voters rush back to Democrats

articles.body: Voters have forcefully rejected President Donald Trump and Republicans, electing Democrats in GOP strongholds nationwide for the first time in decades and turning the GOP’s deepest fears into reality. As generational-level losses stacked up across the country and in the deepest of red seats, Republicans accepted what is on track to be a historic midterm defeat — a long-feared “blue wave” that had started washing across the nation. "Massacre," Rep. Mark Amodei (R-Nev.), who is retiring, said in an interview. The extent of the washout became clear soon after polls closed: Republicans lost a South Carolina Senate seat for the first time in nearly 30 years. Democrats nipped on the heels of House incumbents in deep red Florida districts. And the man in charge of the party’s House reelection effort was at grave risk of losing his own seat. By 11:30 p.m., Democrats had already flipped eight GOP House seats — itself enough to win a majority if Republicans can’t make gains elsewhere — and many in the party feared dozens more could follow as voters registered their dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump. Voters in Texas, a ruby-red state for a generation, elected at least two Democrats to statewide office, flipping the Senate seat and the governor’s mansion. And Kansas Democrats flipped a Senate seat for the first time in nearly a century. As the defeats continued, Republicans — long afraid of a president who has maintained an ironclad grip on the party — said Trump was to blame for their poor electoral performance. “President Trump hasn't exactly done any Republicans favors across the country,” Joe Straus, a former Texas state House speaker, said on a POLITICO election night broadcast. “They haven't done themselves favors, frankly, by following so closely along.” Some didn’t mention the president by name, but it was still clear he was the one taking the blame. "Voters all across America have spoken, and this is a wake-up call for all conservatives," said Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.), arguing the GOP needed to "start governing on the core principles they campaigned on." Trump, meanwhile, denied the results were his cross to bear. “I wasn’t on the ballot,” he said during POLITICO’s election night livestream. “I said, ’Say you’re on the ballot, think about me being on the ballot.’ But they didn’t agree and they didn’t like the candidates in most cases.” Many of the political professionals charged with getting GOP candidates elected in this environment said the results could be potentially historic in nature. One operative predicted a “tsunami,” while another deemed it “the worst electoral defeat in my lifetime and likely in history." At an ill-fated victory party for Senate candidate Michael Whatley in North Carolina, staff were already packing up the room less than two hours after polls closed. Returns showed Democrat Roy Cooper on track to win by as many as 20 points in a race that was supposed to have been tooth-and-nail. Standing in the room, one North Carolina Republican openly pondered what many others in the party had long avoided saying openly — that it was finally time to think about life after Trump. “Trump has done some excellent things, and I appreciate that. But it can't be the party of Trump forever,” said Jonathan Fletcher, a former GOP county chair. “If the Republican Party is going to be serious about winning, we have to be serious about winning people in the middle.” Nearly every state, district and county shows movement toward Democrats, from counties that Trump won three times to blue strongholds where Democrats are improving their margins. County-level data shows Democrats doing on average more than 8 points better than Kamala Harris did in the 2024 presidential race. That is putting Democrats in reach of flipping seats in places that Trump won by double digits two years ago. Democrat Annie Andrews won South Carolina, which had gone for Trump by nearly 18 points. Democrats’ House flips included Kentucky’s 6th District, which Trump won by 15. And seats that Republicans had drawn to be friendlier to them in Florida and Texas largely didn’t flip in their favor. The losses threatened to pile up even after Republican candidates, committees and super PACs spent massive sums in an effort to retain control of Congress — including more than $380 million from President Donald Trump’s political operation. Many Republicans said the war in Iran, which sent voters’ gas prices soaring, and continued frustration with the economy drove frustration with a party that won on those same issues in 2024. On top of that some quickly vented about substandard candidates — such as Darline Graham in the South Carolina Senate race and Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate contest. "Not only were folks upset about the war, inflation and gas prices, but add to that the fact they think he was making them eat a shit sandwich in Darline, and they just had enough," said Mick Mulvaney, a former Trump White House chief of staff and South Carolina congressman. Trump said on Truth Social his own absence from the ballot for the drastic Republican underperformance — even after barnstorming the country begging Republicans to “vote like I’m on the ballot.” “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump posted shortly after 10:30 p.m. Other Republicans were ready to blame Trump’s own decisions. "Republicans got their asses kicked tonight because of the Iran war — plain and simple. Everything else is just noise and spin,” said a person close to the White House. Meanwhile, power in Washington was already shifting. The likely next chair of the House Oversight Committee, who has been gearing up for massive probes into the Trump administration, issued a two-word statement Tuesday addressed to administration officials and the “Trump Crime Family.” “Lawyer up,” Rep. Robert Garcia of California said. Amanda Chu, Will Steakin, Erin Doherty, Lauren Fedor, Ashley Ahn and Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Voters pummel GOP out of power

articles.body: Joe Biden was unceremoniously ushered out of the White House two years ago. On Tuesday, he got a small measure of revenge. Prominent Biden administration alumni are winning in a handful of notable races, with Keisha Lance Bottoms — the one-time Atlanta mayor turned Biden’s senior adviser and director of the Office of Public Engagement — leading the pack by flipping Georgia’s governorship. The victories, his former staffers say, are an important part of rehabilitating his legacy within a Democratic Party that all but banished him in 2024. “It's proof that President Biden assembled a talented team of public servants — who the public is calling on now to help turn this country around,” said Ron Klain, Biden’s former chief of staff. “These fantastic men and women will make life more affordable, health care more available, protect our rights, fight corruption, and make our country stronger.” Biden was not a regular on the trail this year, and most Democrats kept their distance from the former president. But he did weigh in on a handful of primaries, helping put loyal lieutenants in front of voters who still held him in high regard. While Bottoms was the highest profile victory, there’s a number of Biden alumni also poised to head to Washington. Gabe Amo, who won a 2023 special election in a blue Rhode Island seat, secured his second full term in Congress. And Dan Koh, who won Massachusetts’ 6th District to succeed Rep. Seth Moulton, was Biden’s deputy Cabinet secretary and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs. He leaned into his Biden endorsement throughout the campaign and this week reposted a video of a phone call he and his family had with Joe and Jill Biden on primary night in September. “Mr. President and Madame first lady, thank you so much for all of your support,” he told them. “It wouldn’t have been possible without both of you. … You changed my life by giving me a job of a lifetime. And you got my back the minute I decided to run.” Biden’s Cabinet also had a strong night in other governor races. Xavier Becerra, Biden’s secretary of Health and Human Services, had a solid polling lead over Republican Steve Hilton in the race to be California’s next governor going into Tuesday. And, Deb Haaland, Biden’s Interior secretary, was projected to win the New Mexico governor race. "In his farewell speech, President Biden warned that ‘an oligarchy is taking shape in America of extreme wealth, power, and influence that literally threatens our entire democracy,’” said Andrew Bates, the former president’s longtime spokesperson. “He urged his team and supporters to keep standing up for the values that we all care about, including decency, hard work, and a sense of national community. On the ballot and off, a whole lot of his alumni are fighting to carry on that legacy.” CORRECTION: A previous version of this report misstated how many full terms Gabe Amo has served.
articles.headline: Biden’s revenge: His alumni are winning in the midterms

articles.body: Republicans don’t think their party is focused enough on their biggest issue. The economy — and specifically the cost of living — is far and away voters’ top concern, and new results from The POLITICO Poll reveal a warning sign for the GOP just hours before polls close: There’s a stark disconnect between what Republican midterm voters want their party to focus on and what they say the party actually is focusing on. Nearly half of Americans — 47% — say cost of living and affordability are among the issues that matter most when they are deciding how to vote. That includes a 44% plurality of Republican midterm voters and 54% of Democratic midterm voters. The economy and jobs ranked second. But when asked which issues matter most to their party, a 39% plurality of Republican voters cited immigration and deportations as a top priority for the GOP. Just 23% said the party’s top priority was cost of living and affordability — a 21-point gap from the share who said it was a top voting concern. Nearly two-thirds of Republican voters also say they want to hear more about the economy and cost of living from their party. It’s a clear signal that voters wanted the GOP to stay focused on affordability, even as some Republicans and President Donald Trump continued to lean into culture war attacks — from transgender athletes in women’s sports to calling Texas’ Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico “tofu Talarico.” In recent speeches, Trump has often prioritized other topics — including cultural issues, the Reflecting Pool and, yes, GOP candidates’ rear ends — over the economy. If Democrats win the midterms, “you will have a 1929 style economic depression,” Trump told a crowd in Daytona Beach, Florida this Friday. He added immediately after: “Because when you hear men in women's sports, when you hear transgender, when you hear about — you know, open borders and all — everything they have is crazy.” Meanwhile, there isn’t the same dissonance on Democrats’ side: A plurality of Democratic voters pointed to cost of living and affordability as a top priority for their party, the poll found. The findings expose a potential messaging vulnerability for Republicans heading into Election Day: Even among voters planning to support the party, there is a perception that GOP leaders are not devoting enough attention to the cost of living concerns weighing most heavily on Americans. Trump’s own agenda — his tariffs and his decision to involve the U.S. in a war with Iran — has roiled the country and key races that could determine balance of power in Congress. “Well, I don't think it's good for Republicans,” Republican strategist Jeff Burton said of the poll results. “But it makes sense, because most of the Republicans' campaign message hasn't evolved around that and what affordability and cost of living really is. And it's hard to tout it when every street corner has gas prices $2 or more than they were just a few months ago.” The survey, conducted by PF Global the weekend before the election, underscores the messaging challenge that has dogged Republican candidates throughout the cycle. Candidates in races up and down the ballot have zeroed in on economic talking points: Campaigns and outside groups have spent more than $800 million on ads focusing on affordability, including roughly $401 million from Democratic-aligned groups and $311 million from Republican-aligned groups, according to a POLITICO analysis of primarily TV ad data from the tracking firm AdImpact. Still, the GOP has struggled to effectively convince voters that it is doing enough to fix an issue voters also hold them responsible for. Some Republican strategists think that disconnect comes down to one person: Trump. “I mean, look at what he's doing today,” said longtime Arizona Republican strategist Chuck Coughlin on the eve of the election. ”He's going in front of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool. He's drawing attention back to his monument exhibition.” “It's phenomenal how off message he is, and how that has burdened the party with his narrative, which doesn't come close to talking about what Americans care about,” Coughlin continued. “I mean, he's pretty much said time and time again, he doesn't care. You know, he thinks affordability is a hoax.” At the end of last week, Trump made three campaign stops in Florida, South Carolina and Ohio. Across all of those speeches, he spent just over 10% of his time talking about the economy and the cost of living, according to a POLITICO analysis. That’s significantly less than the amount of time he spent talking about culture war issues and other topics unrelated to the affordability crisis. He spent more minutes advocating for Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) to resign and zeroing in on the Dan Sullivan ballot controversy in Alaska than he did talking about prices and inflation, for example. Guns, transgender issues, and renaming landmarks took up more of his focus than taxes, tariffs, and drug prices combined. "President Trump has delivered on his promise to provide relief to hardworking families, securing more than $82 billion in individual tax relief from No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, the Enhanced Senior Deduction, and No Tax on Car Loan Interest,” White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said in a statement. RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre said “Democrats' far-left policies will decimate” Republicans’ progress and that Trump "has criss crossed the nation to drive voters to the polls to support our Republican candidates who will build on these achievements over the next two years." The POLITICO Poll suggests there is relatively little appetite among Republican midterm voters for more discussion of some of the cultural issues that have featured prominently in Trump’s political messaging. Just 10% of Republican midterm voters said they want to hear more about “wokeness and DEI” from the party, when asked to select two issues from a list of options. And only 6% of Republican midterm voters and 5% of Democratic midterm voters identified race, DEI and “wokeness” as among their top voting concerns. By contrast, 64% of Republican midterm voters said they want to hear more about the economy and cost of living and 42% said the same about immigration and border security. The results also underscore just how thoroughly the economy has dominated this election cycle, relegating issues that played prominent roles in past elections — including abortion rights and transgender issues — to the sidelines. “If Republican voters actually feel that their number one issue isn't being addressed, then that is definitely going to affect turnout,” said Burton, the GOP strategist. “And the worry could be that, ‘okay, they turn out, but do they actually vote Democrat or split their ticket?’”
articles.headline: Poll: GOP voters say the party isn’t focused enough on the economy

articles.body: Republicans’ 2024 coalition is cracking in real time. President Donald Trump roared back into office two years ago after making major gains with young voters and Americans of color. Now those key groups appear to be moving away from him amid an unpopular Iran war and his lagging approval ratings, according to new results from the POLITICO Poll conducted by PF Global. Roughly 9% of Trump 2024 voters plan to cast their ballot for a Democrat this year, compared with just over 2% of former Vice President Kamala Harris’ voters who now plan to back Republicans. Underlying that shift is a lack of enthusiasm from two groups central to Trump’s win: Latinos and young people. At the end of last year, 56% of Hispanic Trump voters identified as MAGA Republicans. As of this October, just 37% still do, revealing a frustration with the label that denotes some of the president’s most loyal supporters. At the end of last year, 50% of young Trump voters ages 20 to 29 said they were certain to vote. As of this October, just 38% say this. It’s an alarming sign for the party heading into election night, as Republicans race to save deep-red seats across the map and juice turnout among the MAGA base to avoid unthinkable losses. The scramble on the campaign trail reveals the extent of the concern. Speaker Mike Johnson is making one final campaign swing through South Texas on Tuesday, where Republicans have been racing to assuage Hispanic voters’ concerns over mass deportations and the economy. GOP officials are fretting about the impact of lingering inflation and high prices on working-class voters of all races, including young men they’re scared to death won’t show up to the polls in strong enough numbers. They’re also pouring millions of last-minute dollars into a series of southern states with large Black populations whose voters appear to be surging to the polls in record numbers — like Mississippi, South Carolina and even Louisiana — to shore them up. “The coalition that we built under Trump doesn't fucking exist anymore,” said Gina Swoboda, a longtime Trump ally and former chair of the Arizona Republican Party. The White House has been trying to stem the bleeding within the Trump coalition of voters: The president has barnstormed a series of largely red states and is holding a flurry of tele-rallies in the final days. “Two years ago, Trump and other Republicans had a play with those voters because they were frustrated with Biden and Harris; two years later, things might be less bad than they were two years ago — but they're still concerned,” said Scott Walker, the Republican former governor of Wisconsin and 2016 presidential candidate who now leads the conservative Young America's Foundation. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said Trump has “crisscrossed the country” campaigning for Republicans and drawing a contrast with “the radical-left Democrats.” “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party,” Bis added. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said in a statement that the “Trump administration has delivered on its promises to the American people” and the president “has barnstormed the nation to tout these achievements.” GOP Latino voters start to shed the ‘MAGA’ label The durability of Republicans’ 2024 coalition is a crucial test for the party’s future. Republicans’ inroads with young, Latino and Black voters propelled the party into a trifecta of power in Washington, and keeping those gains will be key to the GOP’s bid to hold onto power. A regression in support from those groups could send Republicans back to the drawing board as they craft a winning formula for the 2028 presidential election. Top Republicans are incredibly worried about losing their grip on Hispanic voters, as they try to stave off a bloodbath in South Texas, losses across key Florida House seats and more. There’s been a 19-point drop between last November and this October of Hispanic Trump voters who identify as MAGA, part of Trump’s core base, according to the poll. While two-thirds of these voters still intend to vote for Republicans in the midterm election, their dissatisfaction with Trump’s agenda is clear. The survey found that Hispanic Trump voters are more likely than non-Hispanic Trump voters to have voted for Democrats in the past decade — and think the Trump administration’s mass deportations are too aggressive. Just one election season ago, Trump romped to victory in South Texas over Hispanic voters’ concerns about the border and the economy; Texas Republicans redrew the congressional map last year to make seats in South Texas even more favorable . But the Trump administration’s heavy-handed immigration enforcement, championed by senior White House official Stephen Miller, has sent Hispanics swinging back, according to four Hill Republicans, who were granted anonymity to discuss internal conversations. It’s harmed what once seemed like prime opportunities to unseat Democratic Reps. Vicente Gonzalez and Henry Cuellar, while endangering GOP Rep. Monica De La Cruz in a newly redrawn district the president won by 18 points in 2024. A group of Hispanic GOP lawmakers have continued to raise concerns directly to Johnson and senior White House officials. “Would I feel better if gas were $2.50 instead of $3.30? Yeah. But good luck convincing a guy things are getting better while ICE is picking up his uncle,” said one Texas Republican strategist, granted anonymity to speak candidly. The White House in response provided statements from Texas GOP Reps. Pat Fallon, Brandon Gill, Ronny Jackson and Lance Gooden defending Miller. “Hispanic Americans will continue to see that the Republican Party is fighting for the issues that matter most to their families, and Stephen Miller is absolutely leading the charge,” Jackson said. Senior Hill Republicans have been trying to salvage the imperiled South Texas House seats in a flurry of visits over the past few weeks. But they privately believe they reached the point days ago where no amount of money would stave off the impending disaster. “It’s the economy,” said Daniel Garza, the president of the Koch-backed LIBRE initiative and a Texas-based Republican strategist. Republicans’ vote share of Latino voters has increased steadily over the last decade, Garza noted, which is a long-term win for the party. But he says independent Latino voters have grown disillusioned since Trump’s return to office, especially on the economy. “I think they had higher expectations,” he added. Young Republicans aren’t certain they’ll vote One year ago, half of young Trump voters were certain they’d vote in this year’s election. But this past spring, that number dropped sharply: the percentage of young people who’d backed Trump who were certain they’d vote dropped by 11 points. As early as March , shortly after the war in Iran began, young GOP supporters began to voice their frustrations that the president had broken a core campaign promise. Other Republicans predicted that if the war lasted longer than a few weeks, its consequences would come back to bite the party at the ballot box. That chorus included influential voices like podcaster Joe Rogan, who has significant influence over young men. He had hosted both Trump and Vice President JD Vance on his show in the lead up to the 2024 election. Some Republicans are concerned that the big-tent team they formed just two years ago has been irreparably splintered — and their lack of a strong affordability message is to blame. “We forgot that we're a populist party,” said one Republican operative in Florida who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the state of the GOP coalition. Areas like South Florida, and Miami-Dade County in particular, were central to Trump’s diverse, big-tent party: the president flipped the longtime Democratic county for the GOP for the first time since 1988 in 2024. “We went from being a very populist, scrappy kind of kumbaya party to this kind of almost elitist Republican Party,” they added. But even as Democrats see the prospect of significant wins and a crumbling GOP coalition, some warn they, too, haven’t found a winning message they can build on in future cycles. “It's like being in a relationship: You break up with someone and you have a little distance, and then you start romanticizing them,” said Michael Ceraso, a Democratic strategist and veteran of Bernie Sanders and Pete Buttigieg’s presidential campaigns. “I think [Democrats] all have recognized, very much in the summer, just to move out of the way. Because we're watching voters being like, ‘I want out of this relationship with Trump.’”
articles.headline: ‘We forgot what it's like to be populist’: Republicans see Trump’s 2024 crumbling

articles.body: Republicans have a trust problem on affordability, and Democrats are poised to inherit it. If Democrats do as well tonight as polls suggest, everyone knows the two reasons why: affordability and President Donald Trump. For a year now, The POLITICO Poll has consistently found that half of Americans rank the cost of living as one of their top three issues — and in a series of surveys this month, most Democratic voters say their vote is more about Trump than the candidates on the ballot. But our polling also reveals the challenges for a Democratically-controlled Congress. Democrats have opened up a strong advantage on affordability, but voters who are demanding action may quickly turn on a party that finds itself torn between competing priorities. Much of the Democratic coalition is approaching the midterms as a referendum on Trump, meaning a victory tonight would offer few clear lessons about what should come next. Democratic voters’ two biggest demands — drive down the cost of living and stop Trump — can also conflict, especially when it comes time to govern. Asked to choose between passing bipartisan legislation to reduce the cost of living or avoid giving the Trump administration any wins, Democrats are not united. Twenty-nine percent would prefer to sacrifice progress on affordability to help their 2028 chances. Here is what a year of The POLITICO Poll tells us about the electorate heading into the midterms — and what comes next. Other issues have risen and fallen, but the cost of living has remained in a tier of its own. Even as global instability rose in the spring, roughly half of Americans still ranked the cost of living among the country’s top three issues. The central test of the midterms has barely changed. Republicans’ problem isn’t just that voters are focused on cost of living – it’s that they increasingly trust Democrats to bring it down. Over the last year, Democrats have solidified support from their own base and made small gains among voters who went for Trump or sat out in 2024. That alone was enough to widen their advantage from 2 points to 17 points. Over half of voters supporting a Democratic candidate say their vote is more about Trump and his performance than the candidates themselves. That sentiment is particularly pronounced among progressives and those who have felt the squeeze of rising grocery and gas prices.This reveals a risk for Democrats. Learning how to beat Trump is less valuable than learning how to run candidates with popular platforms of their own — particularly with only two years left before he is no longer the president. Over the past year, we tested Democratic voters on a series of trade-offs between standing on principle and risking control of the House or the fight against Trump. They agreed on one thing: Lying to win is a bridge too far. Beyond that, Democratic voters are often split between principle and pragmatism. A narrow victory could sharpen the party’s progressive-moderate divide , but the larger question for a Democratic Congress would be how hard to fight Trump’s agenda. Before the 2024 presidential election, PF Global’s polling showed a dynamic that might sound familiar. Trump voters believed nearly every part of American life was getting worse. Now, under a Republican administration, their outlook has brightened — while Harris voters have grown markedly gloomier. The reversal shows how quickly partisan control shapes public perception. If Democrats retake Congress, they may gain not only the power to address voters’ problems, but the burden of solving them. Seb Wride is the head of polling at PF Global, the London-based firm that runs The POLITICO Poll.

ÁLVARO GARCÍA"></img><p>A las 6.30 del miércoles 28 de octubre, un trabajador del centro de control de Adif en Atocha (Madrid) empieza su turno con una reunión de media hora en la que se le informa de cómo marchan las operaciones de alta velocidad hasta ese momento. Poco más de dos horas después, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-31/radiografia-del-sistema-de-seguridad-que-dejo-de-funcionar-antes-del-accidente-de-urda-casi-una-caida-cada-dos-dias.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-31/radiografia-del-sistema-de-seguridad-que-dejo-de-funcionar-antes-del-accidente-de-urda-casi-una-caida-cada-dos-dias.html">el sistema de seguridad LZB</a>, que impide que dos trenes coincidan en el mismo punto, se cae en un tramo de más de 63 kilómetros en la vía de altas prestaciones que une Madrid con Sevilla. Siete trenes se paralizan inmediatamente. Son las 8.30. Ese trabajador de Adif ordena seis minutos después que el AVE 2080 reemprenda la circulación a marcha normal, pese a que el protocolo de aplicación en esa situación especifica que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-30/los-controladores-de-atocha-ordenaron-seguir-el-protocolo-equivocado-antes-del-choque-entre-el-ave-y-el-iryo-me-estaba-liando.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-30/los-controladores-de-atocha-ordenaron-seguir-el-protocolo-equivocado-antes-del-choque-entre-el-ave-y-el-iryo-me-estaba-liando.html">debe ir a una velocidad lo suficientemente lenta (marcha a la vista) como para detenerse</a> si aparece un obstáculo en la vía. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/por-que-han-chocado-dos-trenes-en-toledo.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/por-que-han-chocado-dos-trenes-en-toledo.html">Apenas 17 minutos después</a>, ese convoy, lanzado a entre 160 y 200 kilómetros por hora, se empotra contra un Iryo completamente detenido a las puertas de la estación de Urda (Toledo), provocando al menos 69 muertos y cientos de heridos. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/lzb-ertms-y-cdi-113-200-una-semana-descifrando-los-17-minutos-del-accidente-de-urda.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/A2FUNVTMCREGJIFMQ3QW7QIANM.jpg?auth=a8f736f7312550b7304e861063d1d365f59bf6d1ef83f94076e42c9cd3c4a81f" width="8192" height="4608" alt="El ministro Óscar Puente comparece en la Diputación Permanente del Congreso para informar de las causas del accidente ferroviario de Urda. articles.body: <p>Las<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-30/ultima-hora-y-reacciones-tras-el-accidente-de-trenes-de-urda-toledo-en-directo.html" target="_blank" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-30/ultima-hora-y-reacciones-tras-el-accidente-de-trenes-de-urda-toledo-en-directo.html"> víctimas del accidente ferroviario que ocurrió el 28 de octubre en Urda </a>(Toledo), que ha dejado al menos 69 fallecidos y más de 100 heridos, tienen derecho a una indemnización por los daños y perjuicios sufridos. Además de las <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-30/hasta-84000-euros-para-victimas-con-graves-secuelas-asi-seran-las-indemnizaciones-por-la-tragedia-ferroviaria.html" target="_blank" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-10-30/hasta-84000-euros-para-victimas-con-graves-secuelas-asi-seran-las-indemnizaciones-por-la-tragedia-ferroviaria.html">compensaciones del seguro obligatorio de viajeros (SOV)</a>, de las que puedan corresponder a las aseguradoras de las empresas implicadas, y las ayudas aprobadas por el Gobierno, los perjudicados podrán acudir a los tribunales para reclamar una indemnización por responsabilidad civil. Pero antes, deberán esperar a que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-29/los-cabos-por-atar-del-siniestro-de-urda-en-las-investigaciones-judicial-y-tecnica.html" target="_blank" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-29/los-cabos-por-atar-del-siniestro-de-urda-en-las-investigaciones-judicial-y-tecnica.html">la investigación abierta</a> en la plaza número 2 de la Sección Civil y de Instrucción del Tribunal de Instancia de Orgaz concluya qué fue lo que causó el choque entre el Iryo y el AVE, lo que puede tardar varios meses, incluso años, según varios expertos jurídicos consultados.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-11-05/la-lenta-via-de-los-juzgados-para-reclamar-indemnizaciones-tras-un-accidente-de-tren.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

"></img><p>Por mucho sentido dramático y mucho suspense que le pusiera <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/oscar-puente-dimite-por-dignidad-quiero-estar-a-la-altura-de-mi-pais.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/oscar-puente-dimite-por-dignidad-quiero-estar-a-la-altura-de-mi-pais.html">Óscar Puente a su dimisión</a>, el gesto no resuelve nada ni rebaja la vergüenza de una sesión parlamentaria que puso en escena el oportunismo y la indiferencia de los partidos ante los problemas de fondo. Nada invalida la reflexión que hizo Gabriel Rufián en su primera interpelación al todavía ministro, cuando dijo que la intriga de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/puente-dice-que-comprende-que-le-pidan-la-dimision-pero-sigue-porque-no-ha-tomado-ninguna-decision-que-contribuya-al-accidente.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/puente-dice-que-comprende-que-le-pidan-la-dimision-pero-sigue-porque-no-ha-tomado-ninguna-decision-que-contribuya-al-accidente.html">su cese o su permanencia</a> era una distracción para perpetuar la confrontación política y evitar el único debate necesario: qué modelo ferroviario quiere España. La dimisión de Puente —tardía y con saturación de efectismo, pero no por ello menos justa e inevitable— puede satisfacer las políticas de la venganza y a quienes creen que la discusión se agota en el reparto de culpas, pero no soluciona nada. Ni siquiera parece que pueda propiciar una conversación sobre el sistema de transporte, que determina la cohesión, el carácter y la estructura misma del país. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-11-04/el-debate-sobre-el-modelo-ferroviario-que-nunca-tendremos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p><a href="https://elpais.com/america/2026-02-03/bernardo-arevalo-guatemala-se-juega-la-democracia-en-los-proximos-meses.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/america/2026-02-03/bernardo-arevalo-guatemala-se-juega-la-democracia-en-los-proximos-meses.html">Bernardo Arévalo</a> (Montevideo, 68 años) ha tenido que remar a contracorriente desde que asumió el Gobierno de Guatemala en enero de 2024. Tras denunciar intentos de golpe de Estado para impedir su llegada al poder, el mandatario ha debido lidiar con el desgaste político, gobernar con una minoría en el Congreso, afrontar la suspensión y fragmentación de su partido y luchar para llevar a buen puerto una serie de nombramientos en instancias clave del Estado, como la Fiscalía General y el Tribunal Supremo Electoral. A todo eso se suman las turbulencias, las presiones y las responsabilidades propias del cargo. “Es complicado, pero no imposible”, afirma Arévalo sobre su día a día en la silla presidencial. De visita en Madrid en el marco de la <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/las-ausencias-de-lula-y-sheinbaum-dejan-solo-a-sanchez-frente-a-milei-en-la-cumbre-iberoamericana-de-madrid.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/las-ausencias-de-lula-y-sheinbaum-dejan-solo-a-sanchez-frente-a-milei-en-la-cumbre-iberoamericana-de-madrid.html">XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana</a>, el único presidente progresista de Centroamérica analiza en una entrevista con EL PAÍS la actualidad política de la región y hace balance a poco más de un año de concluir su mandato.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/internacional/2026-11-05/bernardo-arevalo-tenemos-que-oponernos-a-la-normalizacion-del-autoritarismo-y-las-dictaduras.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El Fiscal Superior de Cataluña, Francisco Bañeres, ha denegado el acceso a una investigación reciente sobre un violador en serie a tres de sus víctimas que lo habían solicitado. Tras diversas negativas de Bañeres, una de ellas lo solicitó por escrito el 14 de octubre, tras conocer que se ha obtenido un nuevo perfil genético completo, aunque anónimo, del agresor. Pero dado que los delitos han prescrito, “resulta necesario preservar los derechos fundamentales y los datos personales de terceros”, dice el fiscal en referencia al violador impune cuya identidad podría desvelarse, y añade que la condición de víctima no da “por sí sola, un derecho de acceso” a la investigación. Así consta en un decreto notificado el lunes pasado, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-24/la-fiscalia-de-cataluna-niega-a-tres-victimas-el-acceso-a-la-investigacion-sobre-las-violaciones-que-sufrieron.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-24/la-fiscalia-de-cataluna-niega-a-tres-victimas-el-acceso-a-la-investigacion-sobre-las-violaciones-que-sufrieron.html">dos días después de que EL PAÍS publicase una noticia sobre la falta de respuestas</a>.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/la-fiscalia-de-cataluna-prioriza-el-derecho-al-anonimato-de-un-violador-impune-frente-a-tres-victimas-que-piden-copia-de-la-investigacion.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El sector del ferrocarril <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/las-centrales-sindicales-del-ferrocarril-se-plantean-una-fuerte-movilizacion-para-acelerar-refuerzos-en-la-seguridad.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/las-centrales-sindicales-del-ferrocarril-se-plantean-una-fuerte-movilizacion-para-acelerar-refuerzos-en-la-seguridad.html">está incendiado tras el siniestro de Urda (Toledo)</a>, segundo con consecuencias mortales en un periodo de 10 meses en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/ultima-hora-de-la-actualidad-politica-en-directo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/ultima-hora-de-la-actualidad-politica-en-directo.html">El vicepresidente primero, Carlos </a>Cuerpo, asume este miércoles las competencias <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/puente-se-aparta-para-intentar-salvar-la-campana-del-psoe-pese-al-respaldo-de-sanchez-a-su-gestion.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/puente-se-aparta-para-intentar-salvar-la-campana-del-psoe-pese-al-respaldo-de-sanchez-a-su-gestion.html">a las que renunció anoche Óscar Puente</a> como ministro de Transportes, tal y como ha anunciado en una breve comparecencia el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez. No va a tener tiempo para mucho, más que para apagar fuegos. Urge apaciguar los ánimos entre los sindicatos ferroviarios. El de maquinistas, Semaf, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-01/diego-martin-jefe-sindical-de-los-maquinistas-los-trabajadores-no-confiamos-en-el-sistema-ferroviario.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-01/diego-martin-jefe-sindical-de-los-maquinistas-los-trabajadores-no-confiamos-en-el-sistema-ferroviario.html">tiene convocada una huelga para los próximos 10 y 12 de noviembre</a>, los días antes y después del paro general. El potente colectivo reclama el cumplimiento de los acuerdos de refuerzo del mantenimiento de las redes de Adif y de las plantillas de empresas públicas ferroviarias, también de la agencia de seguridad, firmados en febrero. Fue tras las tragedias de Adamuz (Córdoba) y Gelida (Barcelona), y Semaf se queja de que “las promesas no cristalizan en realidades”, según su secretario general Diego Martín. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/una-crisis-ferroviaria-y-aplacar-a-un-sector-constructor-de-unas-los-desafios-de-cuerpo-tras-la-era-puente.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>“No es ningún drama”, dijo este martes Óscar Puente, refiriéndose a su <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/oscar-puente-dimite-por-dignidad-quiero-estar-a-la-altura-de-mi-pais.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/oscar-puente-dimite-por-dignidad-quiero-estar-a-la-altura-de-mi-pais.html">dimisión como ministro de Transportes</a>, “ni hay que hacer ningún drama de ello. Drama el de las víctimas, el de sus familias, el de los seres queridos que ya no van a volver a ver; los heridos, algunos de ellos maltrechos, amputados... Quiero que todos ellos sepan una cosa: sé que mi dolor no puede en modo alguno equipararse al suyo, pero después del suyo, ninguno, créanme, es tan grande como el mío”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-04/todas-las-dimisiones-del-equipo-de-sanchez-desde-su-llegada-al-gobierno-las-ultimas-tres-en-apenas-20-dias.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El suceso ferroviario de Urda se ha cobrado esta tarde un nuevo cargo de alta responsabilidad, el del presidente del gestor de la infraestructura Adif, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-02/maxima-presion-para-el-cese-del-presidente-de-adif-a-horas-de-la-comparecencia-de-puente-en-el-congreso.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-02/maxima-presion-para-el-cese-del-presidente-de-adif-a-horas-de-la-comparecencia-de-puente-en-el-congreso.html">Luis Pedro Marco de la Peña</a>, que ha presentado su dimisión una semana después de la tragedia. La salida se produce tras un encuentro con el vicepresidente primero del Gobierno, Carlos Cuerpo, que esta mañana <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/una-crisis-ferroviaria-y-aplacar-a-un-sector-constructor-de-unas-los-desafios-de-cuerpo-tras-la-era-puente.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/una-crisis-ferroviaria-y-aplacar-a-un-sector-constructor-de-unas-los-desafios-de-cuerpo-tras-la-era-puente.html">ha asumido la responsabilidad sobre el Ministerio de Transportes</a>. La primera renuncia tras dar explicaciones en el Congreso sobre las circunstancias que rodearon al accidente del pasado miércoles fue la de Óscar Puente, hasta anoche máximo responsable del Gobierno en materia de transporte. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/el-presidente-de-adif-se-reune-con-cuerpo-para-explicar-el-suceso-de-urda-y-poner-el-cargo-a-disposicion.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>“¡Ahí viene!”. El grito de una mujer mayor, subida a un banco y agitando el brazo, rompe la espera en la plaza Mayor de Ciudad Real. Cientos de personas se agolpan para recibir a Santiago Abascal. Algunas llevan más de tres horas aguardando su llegada. La expectación es tal que, cuando aparece el líder de Vox, la multitud irrumpe en el pasillo que la organización había habilitado para facilitar su entrada. Un miembro del equipo intenta despejarlo una y otra vez, pero la gente vuelve a cerrarlo. Cuando por fin consigue llegar al micrófono, Abascal va directo al enfrentamiento político. Su primer mensaje tiene como destinatario a Pedro Sánchez y como motivo el relevo de Óscar Puente al frente de Transportes, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-04/sanchez-encarga-a-cuerpo-la-gestion-de-transportes-para-dar-confianza-seguridad-y-certidumbre.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-04/sanchez-encarga-a-cuerpo-la-gestion-de-transportes-para-dar-confianza-seguridad-y-certidumbre.html">una cartera que asumirá el vicepresidente primero y ministro de Economía, Carlos Cuerpo.</a> “Es solo un cuerpo más que se interpone entre Pedro Sánchez y el banquillo. Solo un fusible más para Pedro Sánchez”, sentencia. Y remata: “Nos atrevemos a decir que la traición de este Gobierno mata”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/abascal-convierte-el-relevo-de-puente-en-un-ataque-al-presidente-siempre-tiene-un-fusible-que-desconectar.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: Primer dia per demanar el Bonus Cultura de 20 € i els usuaris estan tenint problemes amb la plataforma digital habilitada per fer la sol·licitud. L’Ajuntament reconeix que hi ha una incidència amb Gmail , el servei de correu electrònic gratuït de Google, que impedeix demanar aquest abonament . Fonts municipals han explicat a betevé que hi ha problemes en l’entrega de correus des de la plataforma de sol·licitud del bonus als comptes de Gmail dels usuaris. Fins i tot, el web per demanar l’ajut, www.bonusbarcelonacultura.cat , avisa d’aquesta incidència amb un missatge a la portada . S’ha de recordar que la campanya funciona a través d’aquesta plataforma digital integrada en els sistemes de venda dels establiments i equipaments culturals. També et pot interessar Ja es poden demanar els nous Bonus Cultura de 20 €. T’expliquem com fer-ho Redacció 1 minut de lectura S’està treballant per resoldre el problema El consistori també assenyala que un equip de tècnics municipals està en contacte amb l’empresa Google per resoldre la incidència el més aviat possible. Les mateixes fonts municipals han indicat que no tenen dades de les persones afectades per aquest contratemps que s’ha donat precisament en el dia que s’engegava el programa. 55.000 bonus disponibles L’Ajuntament ha posat 55.000 Bonus Cultura de 20 € a disposició dels usuaris. Amb aquest ajut, cada persona disposarà d’un moneder digital amb 20 euros per gastar en espectacles de música, teatre, dansa i circ, sessions de cinema en català i llibres també en català a les llibreries de Barcelona. L’import es podrà utilitzar en una sola compra o en diverses operacions, serà compatible amb altres descomptes i s’aplicarà sempre sobre el millor preu disponible. També et pot interessar Els Bonus Consum, per gastar 10 € en mercats i botigues de barri, es podran demanar el 13 d’octubre Marina Segura i Vidal 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: Feia temps que entitats i grups parlamentaris demanaven un nou protocol d’ús del gas pebre (OC) i aquest dimecres finalment s’ha publicat. Ara bé, lluny de ser una normativa clara i taxativa , segons el Centre per la Defensa dels Drets Humans Irídia és un document que dona carta blanca als Mossos d’Esquadra a emprar l’eina en moltes circumstàncies i tot plegat “ contravé els estàndards internacionals “. També et pot interessar Nou protocol de gas pebre dels Mossos: hauran d’avisar abans de fer-ne ús quan sigui possible Núria Granados 3 minuts de lectura Sònia Olivella, advocada i coordinadora de litigis d’Irídia, critica que, segons l’escrit, el gas es podria utilitzar en espais tancats i també en protestes pacífiques en algunes excepcions, cosa que “ és inacceptable “. Explica que les Nacions Unides ho prohibeixen taxativament en espais tancats perquè “poden causar lesions respiratòries” i en accions pacífiques perquè “seria desproporcionat”. Una altra qüestió que preocupa a Olivella és que el protocol “no preveu cap distància mínima” per ruixar i recorda que no s’hauria de fer servir a menys d’un metre de les persones perquè “poden causar greus lesions als ulls i a la cara”. En tercer lloc, també critica que el document no detalla els supòsits en què es podrà fer servir l’arma per part de la policia: “El redactat diu que es pot fer servir per garantir l’ordre públic i aquesta regulació permet qualsevol circumstància “. També et pot interessar Afectat per l’ús de gas pebre: “Intentava omplir els pulmons d’aire i no podia” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 1 minut de lectura Regulació vaga i ambigua Així, Irídia insisteix que aquesta eina només s’hauria d’utilitzar en cas que hi hagi violència , no “per fer complir ordres ni per dispersar” i que amb aquest redactat es podria utilitzar davant moltes situacions, com “aturar un desnonament”. En aquesta línia, critica que “ regular una arma lesiva amb aquest nivell de vaguetat i ambigüitat és contrari als drets humans ” i que, a més, genera molta inseguretat jurídica . Sobretot, que no s’utilizi l’eina sense revisar el document Amb tot, Olivella conclou que s’ha de revisar el document i que “s’han de canviar aquests preceptes contraris a la regulació internacional”. A més, reclama que no es pugui fer servir l’eina fins que aquesta regulació no es modifiqui, i posa èmfasi en la vaga general convocada per al proper 11 de novembre . Espera, doncs, que la policia no pugui emprar aquestes eines —sota aquesta normativa— a les protestes que es convoquin amb motiu de l’aturada. articles.body: La Unió Esportiva Sant Andreu viu un moment històric tant des del punt de vista esportiu com social. El club andreuenc creix i creix i ha informat que ha arribat a una xifra d’associats que és de rècord i històrica. El número de socis ha arribat als 6.000. Èxit esportiu i social El Sant Andreu viu un moment molt dolç de la seva història. Els èxits esportius i socials venen agafats de la mà. Al terreny de joc els andreuencs han aconseguit dos ascensos en tres anys. Primer va ser de Tercera a Segona Federació, la temporada 2022-23 , i la temporada passada va signar l’ascens de Segona a Primera Federació. De fet, és la primera vegada a la història del club que jugarà a la tercera categoria del futbol estatal. També et pot interessar OFICIAL | L’Europa – Sant Andreu es disputarà al camp de l’Espanyol. Tota la informació Aquest èxits esportius han vingut acompanyats per un creixement exponencial de la massa social. L’afició andreuenca és molt fidel. Com ho demostra la resposta de la gent en els partits al Narcís Sala i també en els desplaçaments a camps com a visitants. En els darrers anys el nombre de socis ha anat augmentant i ara mateix s’ha arribat a una xifra històrica de rècord. El Sant Andreu ha anunciat que té 6.000 associats.
articles.headline: El Sant Andreu segueix creixent: xifra rècord i històrica de socis

articles.body: Cop policial al narcotràfic de drogues sintètiques a Barcelona. Els Mossos i la Guàrdia Urbana han desmantellat un punt de distribució d’aquest tipus d’estupefaents químics que operava a l’Eixample. L’actuació policial ha comportat la detenció d’una persona i la investigació d’una altra per la seva presumpta vinculació amb el tràfic de drogues . A l’operatiu s’han intervingut 244 grams de metamfetamina , 95 grams de ketamina, tusi i GHB i dues balances de precisió. També s’han confiscat 11.000 euros en efectiu. També et pot interessar Dos detinguts per tràfic de drogues en una zona restringida de Collserola Pablo Mena 1 minut de lectura Queixes veïnals a l’immoble La investigació la va iniciar la Unitat d’Investigació de la GUB arran de diverses informacions i queixes veïnals que apuntaven a l’existència d’una activitat continuada de drogues en un immoble. A partir d’aquestes denúncies, Mossos i Guàrdia Urbana van constituir un equip conjunt d’investigació que han finalitzat en l’operatiu que va desmantellar el punt de distribució. articles.body: El Rayo Barcelona BSC s’ha proclamat campió del món de futbol platja després de guanyar la final del mundial davant el Sao Pedro per tres gols a quatre a la pròrroga. El club presidit pel youtuber Spursito aconsegueix el primer mundial per les barcelonines. Adriana Manau va ser escollida com a millor jugadora de la competició. També et pot interessar Júlia Serrat, de vestir la samarreta de l’Europa a l’Olimp del futbol platja El primer títol mundial per a la barcelonines El Rayo Barcelona Beach Soccer Club es va imposar diumenge passat per tres gols a quatre al Sao Pedro en la final del mundial de futbol platja al Main Stadium d’Alanya, a Turquia . L’equip dirigit per Jeroni Rañé va aconseguir la victòria gràcies al doblet d’Adriana Manau i els gols de Joana Meira i Júlia Serrat. En rondes anteriors, el Rayo havia guanyat el Partizanocka i l’Anysport a la fase de grups, al Ceilandia als quarts de final i a les Red Devils Ladies a les semifinals. Amb aquesta victòria històrica en el mundial, el Rayo Barcelona BSC deixa enrere la derrota de fa cinc mesos a Portugal de la final de l’europeu femení contra l’ Higicontrol Melilla , que van guanyar el seu quart títol continental de manera consecutiva. El Rayo Barcelona BSC neix de la fusió de dos clubs Fa dos anys, es van unir el Barcelona Beach Soccer Club i el Rayo de Barcelona per crear aquest equip. Des d’aleshores han celebrat èxits com dos ascensos a Primera Divisió , la Copa Catalunya masculina i el subcampionat d’europa femení. A més, gràcies a uns convenis de col·laboració entre el Rayo Barcelona BSC , el CFS Santakos i la FE Fontsanta Fatjó , el club disposa de 13 categories de formació.
articles.headline: El Rayo Barcelona BSC, campió del món de futbol platja

articles.body: Trens especials que ausculten les vies, càmeres en els combois o un sistema d’arcs instal·lats als túnels. Són algunes de les noves tecnologies que Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) està incorporant per monitorar la circulació del servei de metro i detectar anomalies en temps real. Amb els nous sistemes, l’empresa espera prevenir incidències abans que afectin una xarxa que disposa actualment de vuit línies, 165 estacions i 125 quilòmetres d’extensió. També et pot interessar Prova pilot al metro per evitar inundacions: instal·len barreres de plàstic provisionals Àngels Molina Javier Arilla 2 minuts de lectura Trens que “escolten” les vies El metro genera cada dia un volum massiu de dades recollides per sensors i sistemes tecnològics ubicats en els trens i en tota la infraestructura ferroviària. Una de les eines que proporciona dades clau són els trens auscultadors , una sèrie de combois en circulació equipats amb càmeres i sensors que “escolten” i analitzen contínuament l’estat de la via i la catenària . Aquesta tasca d’auscultar les vies permet analitzar paràmetres com la geometria de la via (l’ample, l’alineació, el peralt i l’anivellament), a més de controlar el comportament de l’acceleració dels trens i la temperatura del carril. Actualment, el tren auscultador està en servei a les línies 1 i 5 del metro . També et pot interessar L’L1 i L5 del metro passaran cada cinc minuts els dissabtes Jordi Escofet 1 minut de lectura Càmeres per analitzar la xarxa Una altra de les novetats és la incorporació en els combois d’un sistema de càmeres d’última generació . Amb aquestes eines, els trens revisaran i aportaran dades sobre l’estat del túnel a temps real a mesura que hi circulen per la via. Aquest procediment digital permet mesurar i avaluar el perímetre geomètric del túnel per sectors específics, de manera que es verifica la distància amb el tren per garantir la màxima seguretat operativa. També et pot interessar Informació en temps real de metro i Bicing en l’actualització de l’aplicació Transporta’m Redacció 2 minuts de lectura Arcs tecnològics als túnels D’altra banda, TMB també instal·larà als túnels de les línies automatitzades un arc de sistemes tecnològics que ocuparà tota la circumferència del forat. Aquest arc s’encarregarà de revisar l’estat de tots els elements dels trens que estiguin en circulació, a mesura que passin per aquest punt. Amb la nova inversió tecnològica, TMB vol fer un pas important en el procés de transformació digital per connectar els milions de dades generades per la seva xarxa amb actuacions de manteniment i operació. A dia d’avui, un 30 % de la xarxa de metro està totalment automatitzada. articles.body: La història recent del Carmel ja es pot consultar en un únic espai digital. La Memòria Documental del Carmel ha estrenat una plataforma web que recopila fotografies, filmacions, publicacions, cartells i testimonis vinculats a la història del barri. El projecte neix amb la voluntat de preservar la memòria col·lectiva del Carmel i posar-la a l’abast dels veïns i de qualsevol persona interessada a conèixer-ne l’evolució. La iniciativa, impulsada pel Pla de barris i dissenyada per l’ Observatori de la Vida Quotidiana , pren com a punt de partida la feina desenvolupada pel Fons Documental del Carmel , una entitat creada per reunir, classificar i conservar documentació dispersa sobre el barri. Entre els materials disponibles hi ha fotografies històriques, enregistraments audiovisuals i la col·lecció completa dels butlletins de l’Associació de Veïns del Carmel publicats entre el 1972 i el 2002. Un arxiu de les lluites veïnals El fons permet recuperar episodis destacats de la història del Carmel, com les mobilitzacions per aconseguir equipaments públics, les reivindicacions per millorar les condicions urbanístiques del barri o la lluita contra el barraquisme . “Es posa a disposició dels veïns una gran quantitat de documents que recorden la història dels anys 70, 80 i 90 i que serveixen d’estímul per continuar lluitant per aconseguir millores al barri”, explica Alejandro Bosque , membre de l’ Associació Fons Documental del Carmel . Per a Custodia Moreno , una altra de les figures vinculades al projecte, conèixer el passat és una manera de valorar les conquestes col·lectives. Considera que la plataforma pot ajudar les noves generacions a entendre com es van assolir moltes de les millores que avui formen part del dia a dia del barri. El carrer de l’Hortal als anys 70, abans de la seva urbanització Més enllà de conservar documents Els impulsors del projecte defensen que la iniciativa no es limita a recopilar materials històrics. L’ objectiu és contextualitzar-los i construir un relat que ajudi a entendre l’evolució social i urbana del Carmel. “Una foto pot ser molt valuosa, però també ho és saber per què els carrers eren d’aquella manera o quin sentit tenien determinades celebracions i reivindicacions”, apunta Iñaki Andrés , de l’Associació Carmel a la Vista . La presentació oficial del web, al Casal de Barri la Barraca, ha servit també per fer una crida a la participació dels veïns. El projecte continua obert a incorporar materials i testimonis per ampliar un arxiu viu que vol preservar la memòria popular del Carmel des d’una mirada comunitària. articles.headline: La Memòria Documental del Carmel estrena web per preservar la història del barri

articles.body: El Barça ja coneix el seu contrincant en l’eliminatòria de vuitens de final de la Lliga de Campions de futbol sala . Serà l’ MNK Olmissum croata. El partit d’anada serà el 23 de novembre a Croàcia i la tornada se celebrarà el 4 de desembre al Palau Blaugrana . També s’ha definit el camí del Barça si es classifica per als quarts de final. Es veurà les cares amb el guanyador de l’eliminatòria entre el Minerva i l’ Stalitsa de Minsk . També et pot interessar Higor de Souza, jugador del Barça de futbol sala: “Tot l’equip pensa a guanyar la Champions” L’equip de Javi Rodríguez ja coneix el camí per accedir a la Final Four de la Champions , que es disputarà a Biel , a Suïssa . El rival del conjunt blaugrana en els vuitens de final de la Champions serà l’Olmissum croat, que va acabar tercer en el seu grup de la Main Round. L’eliminatòria començarà el 23 de novembre a la pista dels croates i la tornada tindrà lloc el 4 de desembre al Palau Blaugrana . Els horaris encara estan per confirmar. A més, si el Barça aconsegueix batre l’Olmissum , s’enfrontarà en els quarts de final al guanyador de l’eliminatòria entre el Minerva i el Stalitsa Minsk . El Barça jugaria el partit d’anada de quarts el 8 de febrer al Palau i la tornada, fora de casa al 19 de febrer. Inici perfecte a la Champions En la Main Round de la Champions de futbol sala, el Barça va disputar els seus tres partits en el grup 1 amb el Semey, el Lucenec i el Minerva , que es podria tornar a enfrontar amb el Barça . Els de Javi Rodríguez van guanyar els tres partits i això va fer que el Barça es classifiqués per a la ronda de vuitens de final amb nou punts i com a líder. L’equip blaugrana només va encaixar dos gols i va marcar 23 gols.
articles.headline: El Barça de futbol sala s’enfrontarà a l’Olmissum en els vuitens de Champions

articles.body: El Futbol Club Barcelona ha oficialitzat la renovació de Raphinha fins al juny del 2030 després que el director esportiu, Deco, ho digués a l’assemblea de socis que el club blaugrana va fer dissabte, 19 de setembre. El brasiler s’ha convertit en un dels jugadors més importants per a Hansi Flick i per a tot l’equip, fins al punt que n’és el primer capità. Raphinha, de menys a més Raphinha signarà aquest dijous la renovació amb el Barça fins al 30 de juny del 2030 . El capità blaugrana té 29 anys —fa els anys el 14 de desembre— i quan finalitzi aquest contracte en tindrà 34. El brasiler va arribar al club l’estiu del 2022 procedent del Leeds i va estar dos anys sota les ordres de Xavi Hernández . Les seves xifres eren discretes: en les dues primeres temporades va fer només 10 gols en cadascuna. També et pot interessar Raphinha, MVP contra l’Aston Villa a la gespa i als micròfons: “No vull parlar de futbol…” Pablo Agudo 1 minut de lectura L’arribada de Hansi Flick va fer ressorgir el brasiler . En el primer curs amb el tècnic alemany va ser el jugador amb més minuts de l’equip. Va disputar 57 partits entre totes les competicions ( 4.659 minuts ) i va marcar 34 gols . En el segon curs, Flick no va poder comptar habitualment amb el brasiler a causa de les lesions. Això va fer baixar el seu rendiment, va jugar només 33 partits amb un total de 2.192 minuts i 21 dianes. En aquest tercer any sota les ordres de l’entrenador alemany Raphinha és un dels jugadors més importants de l’equip, n’ és el primer capità , i les seves xifres són descomunals. A més a més, està donant un alt rendiment en la nova posició de joc que li ha donat Flick. De davanter centre està aconseguint fer oblidar la manca de nou que té l’equip amb la marxa de Lewandowski i Ferran Torres d’aquest estiu.
articles.headline: Raphinha renova amb el Barça: blaugrana fins al 2030

articles.body: La trucada del ministre de Cultura aquest dimarts va agafar “per sorpresa” Cristina Fernández Cubas , que no s’imaginava la notícia que acabava de guanyar el Premi Cervantes 2026 . L’escriptora ha agraït el guardó, que entén com un reconeixement al gènere del relat , al qual ha dedicat gran part de la seva creació literària. Per això, espera que aquesta distinció, que situa l’autora com una de les figures “més importants” de les lletres espanyoles, sigui una empenta per a tots els que es dediquen a aquesta modalitat literària. “Em deien que eren estranys, que canviés els finals” El jurat va destacar “l’originalitat, excel·lència i coherència” d’una obra que ha “renovat el conte contemporani i ha transformat la literatura fantàstica en espanyol”, una aportació que, segons l’autora, té la llibertat amb què ha desplegat una escriptura inquietant, farcida de misteris quotidians , en què sovint es desdibuixa la frontera entre la realitat i la fantasia . Això va fer que no li fos fàcil començar a publicar. “Em deien que estaven ben escrits però eren estranys, que canviés els finals”, recorda l’autora, que ha agraït la confiança que li va mostrar l’editora Beatriz de Moura . També et pot interessar Enrique Vila-Matas, Premi Nacional de les Lletres Espanyoles 2026 Esther Castarnado 1 minut de lectura Escriure sense xarxa de seguretat El premi li ha arribat en un moment d’efervescència creativa , en què Fernández Cubas es troba plenament immersa en l’escriptura, un procés per al qual, assegura, que no té cap fórmula secreta: “Cada conte és com començar de nou, té molt d’aventura” . Tot i que també ha escrit diverses novel·les, confessa que el relat breu és un repte que l’entusiasma: “Les novel·les saben esperar, però els contes són com un amant infidel, si no estàs pendent marxa amb una altra i et deixa penjada”. Segons explica, un mal paràgraf pot enfonsar tot un relat, un fet que la fa sentir “com una artista de circ que treballa sense xarxa”. Una vida dedicada al conte Fernández Cubas és la setena dona a obtenir el Premi Cervantes al llarg de la història. Nascuda a Arenys de Mar el 1945, va publicar el primer volum de contes, La meva germana Elba , el 1980. Des d’aleshores ha publicat una vintena d’obres que li han valgut guardons com el Premi Ciutat de Barcelona el 2009 i el Premi Nacional de Narrativa de les Lletres Espanyoles el 2023. El títol de la seva darrera obra, Lo que no se ve , defineix bé la seva visió literària: “M’interessa més allò que no es veu que no pas allò que es veu”. També et pot interessar Eva Baltasar guanya el prestigiós premi Médicis Étranger Clara Vera Colina 1 minut de lectura
